We aim to be an integral part of Western Montana’s veterinary community, caring for patients that need extra attention and an after-hours presence.

# Oncology

Image: Our technicians working on samples

The oncology service at Sentinel Veterinary Specialists & Emergency offers comprehensive consultations, diagnostics, and treatment plans for animals with all types of cancer. Having a board-certified oncologist with formal residency training and expertise in the field of veterinary oncology means that your pet will have access to the best clinical knowledge and cancer treatment options available.

While it's sometimes easy to think of cancer as a human disease, it also affects animals. 
## The Initial Oncology Visit

Consultation for pet owners with a pet diagnosed with cancer or suspected to have cancer will be by appointment only and include:

  * Reviewing the history and medical record written by the referring veterinarian as well as a physical examination of the pet
  * Recommendation on further diagnostic tests to obtain a definitive diagnosis if needed, and determine if the cancer has spread (metastasized)
  * Discussion of treatment options including surgery, chemotherapy, electrochemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, symptomatic treatment, or a combination of 2 or more treatment modalities
  * Detailed explanation of possible side effects and expected effectiveness of each treatment option
  * Determining the chemotherapy protocol or symptomatic treatment and administering the treatments per protocol
  * Monitoring the patient during and after the conclusion of treatment
  * Telephone or e-mail consultations to the referring veterinarians

To learn more, please call (406) 218‑2800.

##### Company Overview

Bridger Veterinary Specialists & Emergency is a privately owned specialty hospital located in beautiful Bozeman, Montana. # Pilot Program Debuts Infusion Suite at Remote Site, Provides Groundbreaking Opportunity for Rural Communities to Receive Cancer Care Pilot Program Debuts Infusion Suite at Remote Site, Provides Groundbreaking Opportunity for Rural Communities to Receive Cancer Care

Sep 30, 2024

Patients residing in the frontier region of southwest Montana will now have access to cancer infusion services closer to home thanks to a partnership between Barrett Hospital & HealthCare, Bozeman Health Cancer Center, and Montana State University.

The new infusion center, part of the American Society of Clinical Oncology’s (ASCO) Increasing Access to Cancer Care in Rural Montana program, is using an innovative hub-and-spoke care delivery model to provide remote services for patients in the state who are too far from a referral center for convenient and routine day to day cancer care.

The program, which was launched in 2022, increases access for patients within Dillon, Beaverhead County, and the surrounding areas—addressing a long-standing barrier for individuals and their families or support systems enduring extensive travel to larger cities to receive vital treatments.
